ACTUAL CUBIC INTEGRATION BY PARTS AND SECOND VARIATION. Source94, in its transported plaquette-root notation, reads at x for mu<nu:

This is the original covariant identity, not ordinary differences replacing the transports. If C_F maps v to C_p(F,v), direct variation and the original summation-by-parts convention give

Hence eta d0sharp is bounded by a fixed finite shifted difference and gives a local sup bound, NOT a second-derivative norm. In the eta^2 term one eta remains. This is precisely how derivatives of nabla v are avoided; one does not assume a uniform second-covariant-derivative bound for v, F, or H. The C_vsharp d0F and C_Fsharp d0v terms can be bounded directly from the four-link definition of C, so they contain the first two products. The eta-carrying differentiated terms are bounded as shifted products; no unsupported arbitrary covariant-product identity replaces(4).
